name: Sebastopol
description: Sebastopol is a cross domino game for four players (or three in variants) using a double-six set. Players build four arms from the double-six spinner; the first to play all tiles scores the pips in opponents' hands. Game is played to 60 points.

Country/Region of Origin: China

Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6

items.text: Ural (Russia) variant: First deal started by double-six, then 5-5, 4-4 down to 0-0, then cycle. Players may extend arms without completing all four sides of the starting double. A double played face down blocks that arm; if all four arms blocked, game ends and scores as blocked. Double-six alone in hand at end counts 66 pips, 0-0 alone 100; with other tiles they count 12 and 0. First to 101 cumulative points wins. Three-handed: 7 tiles each, draw from boneyard if unable to play.

Three-handed (Berndt): Nine tiles per player, one left in boneyard. Holder of the double-six sets it and draws the boneyard tile so hand stays at nine; play continues clockwise. If no one has the double-six it is in boneyard: turn it to start, same player who began last hand starts again.
